What this page does not claim

  • No confirmed planet. Every dip, signal and feed entry here is a candidate, unconfirmed. Passing vetting is not a confirmation. The match with pi Men c says the planet is already known, not that this run confirmed it.
  • No planet sizes. No stellar radius is stored, so a depth gives only a planet-to-star radius ratio. The Planets page shows the working.
  • No people on the panel. The panel is the Sentinels and the Probes: 2 Sentinels and 3 Probes. Sentinels run on Claude (Anthropic). Probes are deterministic matched-filter detectors. Their weights rest on calibration with 10 planted and 10 empty light curves each, so they are rough.
  • Archive values only. This page claims no detection. A TOI or archive match compares a stored period with published values.
  • No image of the planet. The planet on the Overview is an artist's impression; the field stars on the sky map are decorative.

Sky

Twenty-six days of pi Men.
One planet found again. One dip unexplained.

3,485 stored brightness measurements over 26.0 days. The panel, 2 Sentinels and 3 Probes (no people), marked 7 dips, which the vetting code grouped into 3 signals: 1 passed, 1 flagged, 1 rejected. Each dip is this pipeline's own candidate, unconfirmed as an independent detection; the archive match says the planet is already known, not that this run confirmed it. The stored archive cross-match (docs/results/pi_men_crossmatch.json) finds the lead signal consistent with pi Men c, a published planet: a known planet, not a discovery. Archive values only. This page claims no detection.

Data: The Extrasolar Planets Encyclopaedia (exoplanet.eu), fetched 18 Oct 2026; 8,049 planets with a stored distance, around 5,433 stars. https://exoplanet.eu/catalog/. NASA Exoplanet Archive not used: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request. exoplanet.eu lists as confirmed every object it treats as a planet: bodies up to 60 Jupiter masses (within their uncertainty), published or announced. Its list is broader than the NASA Exoplanet Archive's, which keeps objects up to 30 Jupiter masses from refereed papers. The list includes 9 entries exoplanet.eu names as exocomets. 327 of its 8,376 planets have no stored distance and are not plotted.

        
Not plotted. The feed's stars (TIC 348835438, TIC 349088467, TIC 348770361) have no stored positions, so they are not on this map. pi Men is placed from the dataset, like every other star; pi Men c is the planet exoplan's run recovered.

        
How to read it. Positions: heliocentric galactic coordinates from RA, Dec (J2000) and distance; x points to the Galactic centre and the grid is the Galactic plane. Axis ticks are in light-years (1 pc = 3.262 ly). Colour: the detection method of the earliest planet shown for each star (Method: the first detection method the source lists for the planet.). Size: planets per star. Microlensing distances come from models of each event and are uncertain. The bias in the cloud is where surveys looked and what each method can see, not where planets are. The Milky Way is an artist's impression drawn by the page, not data; the Sun's position in it is approximate.

        
How we classify: by radius when exoplanet.eu gives one, in Earth radii (1 RJ = 11.21 R⊕): Earth-size below 1.25, super-Earth 1.25–2, sub-Neptune 2–4, Neptune-like 4–10, gas giant 10 or more. Without a radius, by mass (or m sin i, a minimum mass) in Earth masses (1 MJ = 317.8 M⊕): Earth-size below 2, super-Earth 2–10, Neptune-like 10–50, gas giant 50 or more. With neither, the class is shown as a dash.

Feed
The feed from the discovery catalogue: 28 entries, 25 of them match a known TOI period. Every entry is a candidate, unconfirmed: a dip the panel marked, not a planet. A TOI match is an archive comparison. Archive values only. This page claims no detection.

      
Feed rule (discover.py): an entry joins the feed when its depth is at most 5,000 ppm and its signal has at least 2 transits. This is an admission rule, not a vetting result.

Sentinels and Probes
Five reviewers.
Each one earns its vote.

        
The panel that marked dips in run tess-pi-men-s1: the Sentinels and the Probes, no people. Sentinels run on Claude (Anthropic). Probes are deterministic matched-filter detectors.

        

      

      

        
        

      

      

      
Sentinels run on Claude (Anthropic). Probes are deterministic matched-filter detectors. Weights come from 10 planted and 10 empty light curves each: too few to separate 0.6 from 0.5.

      
Weights. A reviewer's weight is its calibration skill from injection tests: the true-positive rate on injected transits minus the false-positive rate on empty light curves, floored (calibrate.py). The calibrated weights are stored in docs/results/reviewer_weights_full_panel.json. The weight in this run is the one manifest.json records; when it differs from the calibrated weight, the run did not use the calibrated weights.

      

        
Calibration plane

        
Each reviewer at its false-alarm rate (x: share of empty subjects it marked) and recall (y: share of injected transits it found) in calibration. Point size is its calibrated weight. The lines join points of equal weight, weight = TPR − FPR, floored at 0.05; up and to the left is better. Stored values only.

        
Probe (deterministic detector), not a personSentinel (Claude), not a personsize: calibrated weight

Explorer ›Planets
What each depth would imply, if it were a planet.
One card per star in the run or the feed. Each entry is a candidate, unconfirmed; the ratio below is what its stored depth implies if it were a planet.

      
Radius ratio only. Rp/R* = √depth, with depth as a fraction (ppm × 10⁻⁶). This assumes a full, undiluted transit and ignores limb darkening. No stellar radius is stored in the run or the catalogue, so this page does not convert the ratio to a planet radius in Earth or Jupiter units. Each bar is a ratio scale from 0 to 0.10, the same on every card.

      
Published planets come from the stored archive cross-match (docs/results/pi_men_crossmatch.json), which covers TIC 261136679. The other stars have no stored cross-match, so their cards have no archive box. Archive values only. This page claims no detection.
